transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—thanks for coming in today. What has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come see me?

I’ve been really restless and fidgety all the time, like I can’t sit still without tapping or moving around. It’s starting to bother me at work and in everyday situations, so I wanted to get it checked out.

Along with the restlessness, do you find yourself feeling very anxious or worried a lot of the time—like your mind is racing with concerns—or is it more that your body feels fidgety but your mood and worries are mostly okay?

It’s mostly that my body feels fidgety and I can’t seem to keep still, even when I’m not particularly worried about anything. I do get normal worries here and there, but it doesn’t feel like constant anxiety or racing thoughts.
Do you also have trouble staying focused, organizing tasks, or finishing things you start—for example getting easily distracted at work or making careless mistakes even when you’re trying your best?
Yeah, I do struggle with that kind of stuff. I get distracted pretty easily at work and sometimes miss small details in emails or reports, even when I’m really trying to pay attention.

Have these concentration problems and restlessness been present in some form since you were a child (for example, in school or at home), or do you feel they only really started in the last few years as an adult?
They’ve pretty much been there since I was a kid. I remember having a hard time sitting still in class and getting in trouble for not paying attention or fidgeting before I was even a teenager.
Do you also tend to act on impulses—like interrupting people, blurting things out, or doing things without thinking them through—and has that caused problems in school, work, or relationships?

Yeah, I do that a lot—I’ll jump into conversations and cut people off without really meaning to, or blurt something out before I’ve thought it through. At work I’ve been told I talk over coworkers in meetings, and in my relationships it sometimes causes arguments because people feel like I’m not really listening or giving them space to talk.

In this segment, the patient describes predominantly physical restlessness without pervasive anxiety or racing worries, ongoing distractibility and careless mistakes at work, clear childhood onset of similar symptoms (trouble sitting still in class, getting in trouble for not paying attention), and current impulsive behaviors (interrupting, blurting out) causing functional impairment at work and in relationships. These features further support a persistent neurodevelopmental pattern rather than a primary anxiety or mood disorder, and there is no new evidence suggesting another diagnostic category (e.g., substance use, mood episodes, or primary anxiety). Therefore, F90.0 remains the sole candidate and is further reinforced; no additional candidates are added or removed.

inference_history.note: Initial candidate list based only on the first complaint of restlessness and fidgetiness. At this very early stage, several broad possibilities must be considered: (1) generalized anxiety-type conditions (F41.1) because persistent restlessness and inability to sit still are common anxiety symptoms; (2) panic-related anxiety (F41.0) because some patients describe internal restlessness and agitation around panic, though we lack information about discrete panic attacks; (3) depressive episode (F32.0) because psychomotor agitation can present as fidgetiness in depression, but we have no mood, sleep, or interest data yet; and (4) attention-related/hyperactivity condition in adulthood (F90.0) because restlessness, fidgeting, and difficulty staying still are core features of hyperactivity/impulsivity. No previous candidate list was provided, so nothing has been removed or refined yet. Further history is needed to clarify time course, triggers, associated mood/anxiety symptoms, attention problems, substance use, and medical causes.
